First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}).
$$

Therefore, we can simplify the given expression by rewriting the $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})$ in the numerator, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})}{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} \\  & =2\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}).\end{aligned}
$$
